plan.title: Good to Great
plan.author: Jim Collins
plan.confidence_note: I know this book's research method, core frameworks, and main company examples in detail, though I would avoid quoting precise figures beyond the headline findings.
plan.one_liner: Why do a rare few ordinary companies become truly great, and what can anyone learn from them?
plan.summary: Jim Collins and his research team asked a simple question. Can a merely good company become a great one, and if so, how? They screened more than 1,400 large American companies. They found just 11 that went from average results to stock returns at least three times the market, sustained for 15 years. Then they compared each one with a similar company that failed to make the same leap. The answers surprised them. The winners were not led by flashy celebrity bosses, and they did not rely on bold strategies or the latest technology. Instead they shared humble but fiercely determined leaders. They put the right people in place first, faced harsh realities honestly, and focused on one clear thing they could be best at. Then they pushed steadily, with discipline, until momentum carried them forward.
